label: Late Middle Ages / Great Vowel Shift Begins (1400 – c. 1600)
impact: A major phonetic change that redefined English **pronunciation**, marking the transition from Middle to Early Modern English.

label: The Printing Revolution in England
impact: William Caxton's press drives the **standardization of spelling and grammar** toward the London/Chancery dialect.

label: The Renaissance (c. 1500–1650)
impact: Massive influx of **classical loanwords** (Latin/Greek) to express new concepts in science, art, and philosophy, greatly enriching the English lexicon.

label: Acts of Union (England–Wales) (1536–1543)
impact: Welsh officially suppressed in administration and law; English becomes the sole language of government in Wales.

label: East India Company founded
impact: Early English influence in India begins; first major step in the global spread of English.

label: Union of the Crowns (England–Scotland)
impact: English gains prestige in Scotland, influencing official and literary Scots.

label: Start of American Colonization (Jamestown)
impact: English begins its geographical spread and the development of distinct **North American dialects**.

label: Acts of Union (England–Scotland)
impact: London-centered English strengthens; Scots marginalized in print.

label: Jacobite Rebellion defeat
impact: Gaelic-speaking Highlands face repression; English spreads via schooling.

label: The Age of Dictionaries and Standardization
impact: Samuel Johnson's dictionary published, codifying spelling and usage and influencing prescriptive grammar.

label: Battle of Plassey
impact: British consolidate control in Bengal (English/Urdu influence).

label: First Fleet arrives in Australia
impact: Establishment of **Australian English**; contact with Indigenous languages.

label: Cape Colony British control
impact: English influence in South Africa begins; Afrikaans affected.

label: Act of Union (Great Britain–Ireland)
impact: English consolidates as administrative language.

label: British take control of Sri Lanka
impact: Tamil/Sinhalese under colonial administration.

label: British Raj established in India
impact: English becomes administrative/educational language across the subcontinent.

label: Scottish Education Act
impact: English becomes dominant in Scottish schools; Gaelic use declines further.

label: Colonization in Africa intensifies (1880s)
impact: English, Swahili, Yoruba, Xhosa formalized in administration; establishment of African Englishes.

label: Welsh Intermediate Education Act
impact: Begins revival of Welsh education.

label: Start of World War I (1914–1918)
impact: Introduces widespread new **technical and military vocabulary**; increased contact between British and American English speakers.

label: Start of World War II (1939–1945)
impact: Accelerates the adoption of **American English terms** globally due to US military and media influence; further technical jargon enters the language.

label: Celtic revival movements (1940s–1970s)
impact: Gaelic, Welsh, Irish language revival efforts intensify.

label: Independence of India & Pakistan
impact: Shift from English to local languages in official use; establishment of **World Englishes**.

label: Vietnam War Era (1955–1975)
impact: Exposure to new terminology and cultural concepts in American and global media; US geopolitical focus increases the prominence of American English.

label: African nations gain independence (1960s)
impact: English maintains a role as official language in many nations; local languages gain print presence.

label: Start of the Internet Age / Digital Revolution
impact: Massive influx of **computing and digital terminology**; English becomes the dominant language of early internet and technology.

label: Welsh Language Act (UK)
impact: Establishes the principle of **equal validity** for Welsh and English in public business in Wales, significantly boosting Welsh status.

label: Gaelic Language (Scotland) Act preparation era
impact: Moves toward official recognition of Gaelic.
